decisions.rationale: Talonflame+Aegislash lead shuts down Whimsicott+Gholdengo: Quick Guard blocks Prankster Tailwind/Encore, Wide Guard blocks Make It Rain. Flare Blitz 2x Gholdengo, Brave Bird/Flash Cannon 2x Whimsicott. Back: Garchomp EQ handles Tyranitar/Arcanine; Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump/Thunderbolt covers Tyranitar, Milotic, Basculegion. Aegislash was unused game 1—Wide Guard is a surprise tech.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 strategy: Lead Talonflame+Aegislash vs expected Whimsicott+Gholdengo. Quick Guard blocks Prankster status; Wide Guard blocks Make It Rain/Rock Slide. Flare Blitz 62-140% Gholdengo; Brave Bird (Gale Wings +1 priority at full HP) 2x Whimsicott. Garchomp EQ 2x Tyranitar/Gholdengo/Basculegion (Ghost NOT immune to Ground). Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump can OHKO Tyranitar; Thunderbolt 2x Milotic/Basculegion. Yache Berry Garchomp survives Ice Punch (45-64%). Floette benched: Fairy 0.5x vs Gholdengo and Whimsicott. Overqwil benched: Intimidate triggers Milotic Competitive. If opponent leads Tyranitar instead, Aegislash Flash Cannon 2x and Wide Guard blocks Rock Slide; pivot to Garchomp/Rotom-Wash. Watch for Gholdengo Protect scouting Flare Blitz. Series down 0-1; must win game 2.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott plus Gholdengo gives immediate Prankster Tailwind and strong spread Steel pressure. Milotic is the preferred Garchomp answer and punishes opposing Intimidate, while Arcanine adds Intimidate, priority, and Fire pressure into Aegislash; this balances the major revealed threats.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's revealed roster: Floette-Eternal, Garchomp, Talonflame, Rotom-Wash, Aegislash, and Overqwil. Preserve Milotic as the preferred Garchomp answer when available. Use Whimsicott Tailwind as the primary speed-control plan and preserve Gholdengo for Steel/Ghost pressure. Use Mega Tyranitar selectively, especially into strong Fairy- or Water-type pressure.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Talonflame)
decisions.rationale: Tailwind gives Garchomp/Rotom-Wash crucial speed control for the game. Wide Guard completely negates Make It Rain, Gholdengo's primary spread attack and biggest immediate threat. Whimsicott holds Focus Sash so attacking it is wasted; Prankster Tailwind may also go up but my Tailwind still benefits my slower mons. Safe, high-value setup turn that preserves both Pokemon at full HP.
decisions.notebook: Game2 lead Talonflame+Aegislash vs Whimsicott+Gholdengo. Turn1 plan: Tailwind+Wide Guard. Whimsicott Focus Sash means never try to OHKO it; chip with Brave Bird after Sash broken. Wide Guard blocks Make It Rain and Rock Slide (Tyranitar). Quick Guard blocks Prankster status (Tailwind/Encore/Helping Hand). Gholdengo Power Gem 4x Talonflame—watch if they skip Make It Rain. Shadow Ball 2x Aegislash. Flare Blitz 62-140% Gholdengo; Gholdengo may Protect scout. Garchomp EQ hits Tyranitar/Gholdengo/Basculegion 2x; Ghost NOT immune to Ground. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump OHKO Tyranitar; Thunderbolt 2x Milotic/Basculegion. Yache Garchomp survives Ice Punch 45-64%. Milotic Competitive punishes Intimidate—avoid Overqwil vs Milotic. If opp leads Tyranitar: Flash Cannon 2x, Wide Guard blocks Rock Slide, pivot Garchomp/Rotom-Wash. Series down 0-1; must win game2.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp's EQ hits Gholdengo 2x and outspeeds it under Tailwind, applying immediate offensive pressure alongside Aegislash's Shadow Ball threat. Garchomp takes Shadow Ball neutrally, unlike Aegislash. Yache Berry insures against Ice Punch from Tyranitar. Rotom-Wash lacks SE coverage vs either active foe and Will-O-Wisp is useless vs Good as Gold. Need aggression down 0-1.
decisions.notebook: Gholdengo confirmed Life Orb + Power Gem usage; Good as Gold blocks all status (Will-O-Wisp useless on it). Whimsicott Focus Sash intact—never plan OHKO; break Sash with priority/chip first. Prankster Encore can lock a switched-in mon; prefer sending mons whose best move is Encore-proof (EQ Garchomp fine). Both Tailwinds up early; speed control mirrors. Garchomp EQ 2x covers Gholdengo/Tyranitar/Arcanine/Basculegion. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump OHKOs Tyranitar; Thunderbolt 2x Milotic/Basculegion. Wide Guard blocks Make It Rain & Rock Slide. Quick Guard blocks Prankster status. Aegislash Shadow Ball 2x Gholdengo; Flash Cannon 2x Whimsicott/Tyranitar. If opp switches Tyranitar in: Flash Cannon 2x, pivot to Garchomp/Rotom-Wash. Milotic Competitive punishes Intimidate—never bring Intimidate user vs Milotic. Series format: must win game2 to force game3; prioritize aggressive plays over passive scouting.

decisions.rationale: Tailwind establishes speed control before either foe can move. Power Gem targets Talonflame’s 4× weakness and, with Life Orb, has a strong chance to OHKO through Charti Berry; removing Gale Wings pressure is the priority. Helping Hand would improve the KO odds but sacrifices Tailwind and leaves the team vulnerable to the opponent’s own speed control.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Milotic as the preferred Garchomp answer when available. Use Whimsicott Tailwind as the primary speed-control plan and preserve Gholdengo for Steel/Ghost pressure. Use Mega Tyranitar selectively into strong Fairy- or Water-type pressure. Prioritize removing Talonflame when possible because Gale Wings and Tailwind create immediate tempo pressure.

decisions.rationale: Earthquake pressures Gholdengo, breaks Whimsicott's Focus Sash, and hits switch-ins. Switching Aegislash to Rotom-Wash dodges likely Prankster Encore and makes a predicted single-target Shadow Ball fail; Rotom resists Make It Rain and is immune to Earthquake. Aegislash's protection is unreliable after Wide Guard, and attacking with it risks being removed before moving. This keeps Rotom healthy for Tyranitar/Milotic while staying aggressive.
decisions.notebook: Durable: opponent Gholdengo is Life Orb Modest with Good as Gold, so status moves fail on it. It has shown willingness to use single-target coverage instead of Make It Rain when Wide Guard is likely. Offensive max-Speed Gholdengo is KOed by Garchomp Earthquake after chip; HP/SpA bulky variants can survive and retaliate, especially with Helping Hand Make It Rain. Whimsicott is Prankster with Focus Sash: never plan an OHKO until Sash is broken; break it with Earthquake/chip, then finish it. Prankster Encore punishes predictable Aegislash; switching the Encore target or using a mon with no prior move avoids it. Aegislash protection chains are unreliable after using Wide Guard, so prefer attacking or pivoting over repeated protection. Rotom-Wash is a key pivot: Levitate pairs safely with Garchomp Earthquake, resists Make It Rain, and answers Tyranitar with Hydro Pump; Thunderbolt pressures Milotic/Basculegion and finishes weakened Gholdengo. Opponent back line: Tyranitar likely Mega and weak to Ground/Fighting/Steel; Milotic has Competitive, so avoid Intimidate into it; Arcanine Intimidate can help but must not enable Milotic; Basculegion is pressured by Electric. Preserve Rotom for the mid-game; use Tailwind to keep Garchomp and Rotom ahead.

decisions.rationale: Encore Aegislash’s revealed Wide Guard, locking it out of offensive pressure while preserving the option to attack it next turn. Gholdengo Protects against the likely Garchomp Earthquake and Aegislash Shadow Ball, preserving our key Steel/Ghost attacker and avoiding a potentially decisive double-target knockout.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Milotic as the preferred Garchomp answer. Use Whimsicott Tailwind as the primary speed-control plan and preserve Gholdengo for Steel/Ghost pressure. Use Mega Tyranitar selectively into strong Fairy- or Water-type pressure. Prioritize removing Talonflame when possible because Gale Wings and Tailwind create immediate tempo pressure. Revealed opponent information: Garchomp carries Yache Berry and Rough Skin; Aegislash carries Leftovers, Stance Change, and Wide Guard; Talonflame’s Charti Berry was consumed.

decisions.rationale: EQ+Thunderbolt focus fire mathematically KOs 90% Gholdengo: min combined roll ≈91.2% of its max HP, and both my actives outspeed it, so it faints before moving. Thunderbolt over Hydro Pump for 100% accuracy. Whimsicott's Encore only locks Garchomp into Earthquake—the move I chose anyway—and Moonblast can't OHKO Garchomp (max 85%). Helping Hand is wasted since Gholdengo dies before attacking. If Gholdengo chains Protect at reduced rate, EQ still chips Whimsicott.
decisions.notebook: Format type chart: Water and Electric are NEUTRAL on Gholdengo (verified 1x), unlike standard chart. Garchomp (200 Atk) EQ is 59.8-107.4% vs Gholdengo (spread 0.75x applied); Rotom-Wash (172 SpA) Thunderbolt is 31.4-58%, Hydro Pump (Mystic Water) 46.4-84% but 80% acc. EQ+Thunderbolt guarantees KO on Life Orb Gholdengo from 90% HP; use this focus-fire rule. Whimsicott Focus Sash is broken; Iron Head from Garchomp is only 53.9-102.2%—not a guaranteed KO on bulky spreads, so pair with chip. Whimsicott Moonblast maxes at 85.4% vs Garchomp—Garchomp always survives one. Gholdengo Shadow Ball does 61-89% to Rotom-Wash: never leave Rotom in Shadow Ball range when low. Gholdengo is slower than both Garchomp and Rotom even under its Tailwind (max 272 vs 276/308). Opponent chains Protect on Gholdengo; success decays, and failed Protect = Gholdengo dies. Whimsicott likely max-Speed Timid (faster than both mine under Tailwind); Prankster Encore targets the last move used—switching in a fresh mon or being locked into EQ are the counters. Back-line plan: Tyranitar likely Mega, weak to Ground (EQ) and Steel; keep Rotom healthy to Hydro Pump it. Milotic Competitive—never bring Intimidate-triggering plays into it. Arcanine Intimidate is an opportunity vs Garchomp but feeds Milotic if both are out. Basculegion pressured by Thunderbolt. Preserve Rotom as mid-game pivot; Aegislash walls Whimsicott/Gholdengo (Moonblast immune) but avoid predictable entries vs Prankster Encore.

decisions.rationale: Encore locks Garchomp into its previously used Earthquake, preventing Dragon Claw or Iron Head and preserving Whimsicott’s position. Switch Gholdengo to Milotic before the spread attack, avoiding a super-effective Earthquake and establishing the preferred Garchomp answer while retaining Gholdengo for later Steel/Ghost pressure.
decisions.notebook: Continue prioritizing Encore-based disruption when an opponent is locked into a poor spread move. Preserve Milotic as the primary Garchomp answer and Gholdengo as the Steel/Ghost pressure piece; use Tailwind proactively when its duration is ending. Track Aegislash’s Wide Guard and Leftovers, Garchomp’s Yache Berry/Rough Skin, and Talonflame’s consumed Charti Berry.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is Encored into Earthquake. EQ KOs Milotic unless it Protects, so Rotom shouldn't waste Thunderbolt there; instead Thunderbolt Whimsicott. EQ+Thunderbolt gives a high KO chance on Whimsicott, and any survivor is within guaranteed Thunderbolt/Aegislash Flash Cannon range. Whimsicott can't OHKO Garchomp; if Milotic Protects, we still chip/KO Whimsicott. Switch Garchomp out next turn if hurt.
decisions.notebook: Format chart: Water/Electric are neutral on Gholdengo. Garchomp EQ is the primary Milotic finisher unless Milotic Protects; Rotom Thunderbolt on Milotic is usually wasted when Garchomp EQ acts first. Against Whimsicott, EQ+Rotom Thunderbolt is the preferred focus; Hydro Pump gives a higher KO roll but 80% accuracy is worse for consistency. Whimsicott Moonblast cannot OHKO Garchomp (max 85.4) and only 33-52 Rotom; Milotic Ice Beam is 42-63 into Yache Garchomp. Plan: if Garchomp takes a big Moonblast, switch it to Aegislash next turn; Aegislash Flash Cannon OHKOes Whimsicott and Shadow Ball finishes weakened Milotic. Expect Milotic Protect and Prankster Tailwind/Encore from Whimsicott; under refreshed foe Tailwind Rotom can be slower than Milotic, so do not rely on Rotom to outspeed and Recover-race. Keep Rotom healthy: Gholdengo Shadow Ball can heavily damage it. Gholdengo dies to EQ+Thunderbolt focus; failed Protect is fatal. Tyranitar fears EQ; Arcanine's Intimidate/Shuca can tank EQ but fears Hydro Pump; Basculegion fears Thunderbolt. Never bring Intimidate into Competitive Milotic. Aegislash checks Whimsicott/Gholdengo but is slow; use it as a pivot, beware Encore locking Rotom.

decisions.rationale: Encore Rotom-Wash into its last-used Thunderbolt, while Milotic Protects against the encored Garchomp Earthquake and Rotom Thunderbolt. This preserves Milotic as the Garchomp answer, avoids losing it at 10% HP, and leaves both foes constrained for the next turn.
decisions.notebook: Continue prioritizing Encore to lock opponents into poor or exploitable moves, especially spread attacks and predictable Electric attacks. Preserve Milotic as the primary Garchomp counter and Gholdengo as Steel/Ghost pressure. Track Aegislash’s Wide Guard and Leftovers, Garchomp’s Yache Berry/Rough Skin, and Talonflame’s consumed Charti Berry.

decisions.rationale: Switch Whimsicott to Gholdengo: it is immune to Encore-locked Garchomp Earthquake, while Arcanine would be vulnerable. Milotic should pass, preserving its remaining resources and avoiding an unnecessary action.

Both Encored: Garchomp must EQ, Rotom must Thunderbolt. EQ KOs Milotic at 16% (min 28.7%). EQ+Thunderbolt KOs Gholdengo at 90% (min combined 91.2%). Garchomp outspeeds all; Make It Rain can't OHKO Garchomp (max 82.2%). Only risk is Protect, but Gholdengo's Protect was used turn 2 and Milotic's is at 50%. Even if one Protects, we're favored next turn when Garchomp's Encore expires.
decisions.notebook: Durable damage calcs: Garchomp EQ KOs Milotic up to ~28% HP. EQ+Rotom Thunderbolt KOs Gholdengo from 90% (91.2% min combined). Life Orb Gholdengo Make It Rain: 56.8-82.2% to Garchomp, no OHKO. Shadow Ball: 61.4-89% to Rotom, no OHKO but critical threat. Milotic Ice Beam: 42.2-63.8% to Yache Garchomp. Garchomp (154) outspeeds all foes; Rotom (138) outspeeds Gholdengo (max 136) and Milotic (max 133). Foe back-line: Tyranitar (Mega, Sand Stream, fears EQ 2x), Arcanine (Intimidate/Shuca, fears EQ 2x), Basculegion (Adaptability/Mystic Water, fears Thunderbolt 2x). Aegislash is the pivot: Steel/Ghost resists Make It Rain 0.5x but takes 2x from Shadow Ball; use Wide Guard/King's Shield carefully. Rotom Encore lasts through turn 6; plan Thunderbolt targets accordingly. Never switch into Competitive Milotic with an Attack-dropping ability. Gholdengo Good as Gold blocks status—only direct damage works. Prioritize eliminating Gholdengo before it gets Shadow Ball on Rotom.

decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Gholdengo from the locked Earthquake while Milotic switches out before the locked Thunderbolt can finish it. Arcanine’s Intimidate weakens Garchomp’s spread attack on entry, giving the replacement a chance to withstand both attacks and preserving Gholdengo for endgame pressure.
decisions.notebook: Encore remains a major control plan: Garchomp is locked into Earthquake and Rotom-Wash into Thunderbolt. Preserve Milotic when possible as the primary Garchomp counter, but avoid leaving it exposed to Rotom’s Electric attacks. Gholdengo remains the key Steel/Ghost attacker; account for Aegislash’s Wide Guard and Leftovers, Garchomp’s Yache Berry/Rough Skin, and Talonflame’s consumed Charti Berry.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp EQ hits both foes (spread); Rotom is Encore-locked into Thunderbolt so must attack. Focusing Gholdengo: combined EQ(35-79%)+Thunderbolt(29-65%)=64-144% vs its 90% HP—decent KO odds, and Gholdengo's Protect success is reduced so it's less likely to block. Arcanine also takes EQ chip. Gholdengo is the top threat (Shadow Ball 50-89% to Rotom). Speed order favors us: Garchomp 154 > Rotom 138 > Gholdengo ≤136, so both hits land before Gholdengo moves.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp at -1 Atk (Intimidate) reduces EQ significantly: vs Gholdengo 35-79%, vs Arcanine 40-91% (spread). Rotom Thunderbolt: vs Gholdengo 29-65%, vs Arcanine 31-70%. Combined EQ+TBolt vs Gholdengo at -1: 64.5-143.8% (not guaranteed KO from 90%). Arcanine Protect has full success rate; Gholdengo Protect is unreliable after consecutive use. Rotom Encore expires after turn 6—free move choice turn 7+. Gholdengo Shadow Ball: 50-89% to Rotom (Life Orb). Make It Rain: 47-82% to Garchomp, 0.25x to Rotom. Milotic at 16% back-line, easy cleanup. Foe back-line: Tyranitar (Mega, Sand Stream, weak EQ 2x), Basculegion (Adaptability Mystic Water, weak Thunderbolt 2x). Aegislash pivot: resists Make It Rain 0.5x but 2x weak Shadow Ball; use Wide Guard/King's Shield carefully. Never switch into Competitive Milotic with Atk-dropping ability. Gholdengo Good as Gold blocks status—direct damage only. Prioritize Gholdengo > Arcanine > Milotic.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Gholdengo from the forced Thunderbolt and the locked-out Earthquake attempt, despite reduced success. Arcanine’s priority Extreme Speed chips Rotom-Wash before it can act; switching risks exposing Milotic to both Earthquake and Thunderbolt, while attacking with Gholdengo likely loses it.
decisions.notebook: Encore remains a strong control plan against forced moves; track its expiration before relying on it. Preserve Milotic for Garchomp when it can avoid Rotom-Wash’s Electric attacks. Gholdengo is the primary Steel/Ghost attacker, but account for Wide Guard, Yache Berry, Rough Skin, and defensive items. Protect may have reduced success immediately after use.

decisions.rationale: Send the sole remaining Pokémon, Milotic, into slot 1; slot 2 has no available replacement and must remain empty.
decisions.notebook: Milotic is the only remaining Pokémon. Preserve it against Garchomp while respecting Rotom-Wash’s Electric pressure; prioritize Protect or Recover when needed, and avoid relying on Encore, which has expired.

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt does 50-84% of Milotic's max HP vs its current 16%—guaranteed KO before it can Recover (Rotom outspeeds). EQ chips the incoming mon (33-59% vs Tyranitar 2x, 22-40% vs Basculegion neutral) while Rotom is immune via Levitate. This secures a 2v1 endgame regardless of which back-liner enters.

For game 3: expect Intimidate lead, protect Garchomp from IcePunch, use Aegislash as Tyranitar check.

decisions.rationale: Protect is mandatory: Rotom-Wash’s Thunderbolt is guaranteed to KO Milotic from 16%, while Recover occurs after Rotom and cannot save it. Protect blocks both opposing attacks and preserves the only remaining Pokémon for a possible follow-up turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Garchomp is Adamant with Yache Berry and has shown Earthquake; its Attack is currently reduced by Intimidate. Opponent’s Rotom-Wash is Modest, holds Mystic Water, has Levitate, and has shown Thunderbolt. Preserve Milotic against Electric pressure; use Protect to scout or create a recovery opportunity, and avoid assuming Ice Beam immediately KOs Garchomp through Yache Berry.

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt guarantees KO on Milotic at 22% (min roll 50.5% > 22% HP); Rotom outspeeds so Milotic can't Recover first. Protect success rate is reduced, making it unreliable for Milotic. Garchomp EQ hits the incoming Tyranitar/Basculegion switch-in for chip (30-66% vs Ttar, 19-45% vs Basculegion) while Rotom is immune via Levitate. Both our mons outspeed all incoming threats.

Basculegion weak Thunderbolt 2x; Wave Crash Adaptability+MysticWater devastating vs Garchomp(1x) but Rotom resists(0.5x). Aegislash good pivot vs both back-liners. selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Protect is the only reliable way to avoid the established Earthquake plus Thunderbolt pressure at low health. It also scouts whether either foe changes plans; attacking does not secure a knockout, while Recover is vulnerable to both faster attackers.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Garchomp is Adamant with Yache Berry, Rough Skin, and has used Earthquake; Intimidate has reduced its Attack. Opponent Rotom-Wash is Modest with Levitate and Mystic Water, and has revealed Thunderbolt. Prioritize preserving Milotic against Electric pressure; use Protect to scout or create a recovery opportunity, and do not assume Ice Beam immediately KOs Garchomp through Yache Berry.

reflections.summary: Won because the Garchomp/Rotom-Wash core exploited a Protect-heavy team with continuous Earthquake and Thunderbolt pressure; the four non-Mega brings matched the opponent's actual four, and their Protect chains failed before Milotic could stabilize.
reflections.adjustment: For game 3, if Tyranitar/Basculegion return, center the preview on Rotom-Wash and Aegislash, scout with Protect/Wide Guard, keep Garchomp away from Intimidate and Ice Punch, and double-attack Milotic before it can Recover.
reflections.notebook: Opponent leans on Protect/Intimidate tempo: Prankster Whimsicott enables, Gholdengo and Milotic Protect predicted attacks, Arcanine provides Intimidate and Extreme Speed. Consecutive Protect can fail; attacking through it with double pressure works. They benched Tyranitar and Basculegion in game 2; expect them in game 3, possibly Mega Tyranitar. Future plan: preserve Aegislash/Rotom-Wash as Tyranitar/Basculegion answers, scout before committing Garchomp, avoid giving Milotic free Recover turns, and use Garchomp/Rotom as the primary win condition when their Protect structure is exposed.

reflections.summary: Lost primarily because the preview plan brought Arcanine and Gholdengo into a Garchomp–Rotom core that could repeatedly combine Earthquake with Thunderbolt. The four lacked sustained pressure after Whimsicott fell; this was a matchup/composition issue rather than a recorded decision error.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Arcanine with Floette-Eternal and make Floette the Mega holder. Bring Whimsicott/Gholdengo/Milotic/Floette, using Mega Floette’s Moonblast or Energy Ball to pressure Garchomp and Rotom instead of relying on Intimidate and passive Protect cycles.
reflections.notebook: Opponent has repeatedly paired Garchomp Earthquake with Rotom-Wash, whose Levitate makes the Ground spread safe and creates strong pressure against grounded partners. Rotom favors Thunderbolt into weakened or exposed targets. Do not rely on repeated Protects for stabilization; preserve a Pokémon that can actively pressure Rotom and Garchomp. Future plan: consider Mega Floette as the primary answer to this pairing, while retaining enough counterplay for Aegislash.
